title: Probe configured FFmpeg encoders in wizard
summary: Make the Settings Wizard encoder probe enumerate configured FFmpeg encoders instead of returning a static advisory result.
reason: Deployment review found that Probe Encoders can report success without confirming whether the configured FFmpeg exposes NVENC or CPU fallback encoders. A non-developer fresh-package user needs a bounded, concrete toolchain signal before launch.
behavior_before: Probe Encoders always returns ok with no detected encoder list and a generic advisory warning.
behavior_after: Probe Encoders validates the configured FFmpeg path, runs a bounded `-hide_banner -encoders` probe, parses video encoder names, reports NVENC and common CPU fallback encoders separately, and blocks missing or failed FFmpeg probes while clearly stating that it does not run a real encode.
tests_added: Settings Wizard Probe Encoders parses configured FFmpeg encoder output into detected, NVENC, and CPU fallback encoder lists.
Settings Wizard Probe Encoders blocks a missing configured FFmpeg path instead of returning a static ok result.
manual_validation: git diff --check for MP-CHANGE-2026-0613-012 touched paths - passed

Actual bundled FFmpeg wizard probe against ops/pipeline/tools/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe - passed: ok=True; NVENC encoders av1_nvenc,h264_nvenc,hevc_nvenc; CPU fallback encoders libaom-av1,libsvtav1,libx264,libx265,mpeg4
rollback_plan: Revert the Settings Wizard encoder-probe implementation, focused tests, summaries, and this change packet.
notes: Scope is bounded to toolchain capability reporting. Do not change FFmpeg command generation, codec policy, media routing, queue launch behavior, source/scratch/output movement, or publish/drain behavior.
